content: LLM agents can trigger duplicate side-effecting tool calls two ways: the LLM itself re-invokes the tool (e.g. after seeing an ambiguous/error result), or infra-level retry logic re-sends after a timeout when the first call actually succeeded server-side. Idempotency keys should be scoped to the unit of external side effect (e.g. one handoff of one lead), not the inference call, and should be derived from stable business identifiers (lead id + target agent + a monotonic attempt marker) so the destination can recognize and no-op a duplicate delivery within a bounded window, returning the original result instead of re-executing.
